content.text:
The three notes are recorded. Here is the story:

**The Last Light of Harrow Point**

Elias Thorne had tended the Harrow Point lighthouse for thirty-one years. He knew every groan of its iron stairs and every mood of the sea below.

Tonight the sea was angry. A storm had rolled in at dusk, and the waves hit the rocks hard enough to shake the tower. Elias climbed the spiral stairs, one hundred and twelve steps, his knees complaining the whole way. At the top he checked the great lens. It turned slowly and steadily, throwing its beam across the black water.

The company had sent a letter last month. The light would be automated, and a machine would replace him. They thanked him for his service. He had folded the letter into his pocket and not mentioned it to anyone, because there was no one to mention it to.

Near midnight he saw something on the water: a small flicker, low and uncertain. A fishing boat, tossed like a cork, was drifting toward the rocks. Elias grabbed the radio and called out, but only static answered. So he did the one thing he could. He opened the shutters wide and swung the lamp by hand, so the beam swept slowly over the reef and marked the safe channel.

For three hours he worked the lamp, his arms burning. Slowly the little boat's light turned, edged into the channel, and slipped past the rocks into the sheltered bay.

At dawn, a young fisherman climbed the cliff path, soaked and shaking. "Your light," he said. "I couldn't see anything else. It led me home."

Elias smiled and looked out at the calm gray water.

Machines could turn a lens, he thought. But someone had to *watch*.

He took the letter from his pocket, looked at it once, and tucked it away. Then he went to make tea.
